Title: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Mixed After A Democratic Sweep In Midterms: NVDA, MU, SNDK, NBIS, IREN In Focus
Author: Aashika Suresh   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 3:55 AM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-11-05T02:55:24+00:00
=== BODY ===
Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats, 24 House districts, five governorships, and twelve state legislative chambers.
They secured an early reported majority of at least 231–141 in the House and 54–44 in the Senate.
Oil prices declined sharply as expectations for the end of the Iran war rose.
U.S. stock futures were mixed overnight late Wednesday as markets awaited the final results of the November midterms even as the Democrats swept both chambers of Congress.
As of 09:30 p.m. EST, Dow futures gained 0.24%, while the S&P 500 futures were down 0.04% and Nasdaq-100 futures fell 0.46%.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
On Wednesday, all three U.S. benchmark indexes rallied on the blue tidal wave. The Dow Jones Industrial Average led the climb, adding more than 1,500 points to close 3% higher. The S&P 500 gained 1.58% at close, while the Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.44%.
Markets welcomed a Democratic victory in early voting counts on Wednesday, sending stocks higher on anticipation of a potential end to the Iran war and expectations of an improvement in economic policy as well as an end to Trump's tariffs.
The Nov. 3 U.S. midterm election results flipped control in both chambers of Congress, with Democrats in the lead.
While final results are still being counted, Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats, 24 House districts, five governorships, and twelve state legislative chambers, securing an early reported majority of at least 231–141 in the House and 54–44 in the Senate. Key red states including Texas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine, and Kansas also flipped blue, making history.
Consumer discretionary names such as Walmart gained following the initial counting. However, AI-lined and data center build-out names trended lower as markets expect a pullback in support to the industry amid Democratic leadership.
Yorkville Advisors partner and managing director Dan Ives said in a post on X, "Democratic blue tidal wave across the Senate and House was a seismic shift that will have a negative impact on the pace of the AI Revolution buildout in the US over the next few years. Will slow the pace of the planned 800 to 1,000 datacenters across the US fueling the AI Revolution…some investors will like the "slower pace"…others view it as adding risk. We estimate 10% of datacenters will not happen now."
However, Fundstrat's Tom Lee took an opposing stance, saying in an interview with CNBC on Wednesday that Democratic gains in the midterms could prove positive for stocks and lead to a 15-20% rally in tech stocks, calling Wednesday's tech selloff a "knee-jerk reaction."
Oil prices declined sharply as expectations over the end of the Iran war rose. Brent crude futures were trading at $93.91 a barrel, down about 0.75%, while WTI crude futures traded 1% lower at $87.24 per barrel.
Markets will now be watching for weekly jobless claims data and October's nonfarm payrolls report later this week.
On the earnings front, Toyota Motor Corporation, ConocoPhillips, Sony Group, Airbnb, and Cloudflare are among the top companies reporting their quarterly results on Thursday.
Nvidia Corp. (NVDA): The AI darling was on top of the retail radar after a 3% decline in shares as investors were concerned about tighter AI data center rules and delays in AI buildouts amid a Democratic win.
Micron Technology Inc. (MU): The chipmaker's stock plunged 7% at close on Wednesday and continued to decline overnight amid growing concerns for AI-linked names following the early midterm election results.
Sandisk Corp. (SNDK): The memory stock plunged nearly 8% at close on Wednesday and dipped further overnight amid similar concerns for tightened AI policy following a blue tidal wave.
Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS): The election results also weighed on shares of this AI infrastructure company, with the stock dropping more than 6% at close and down by nearly 3% overnight.
IREN Ltd. (IREN): The company garnered attention after The Information reported on Wednesday that Microsoft's lower-than-expected AI data center spending was partially caused by the delays from the Australian cloud computing infrastructure provider.
Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) were down at the time of writing, while the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged higher.
Meanwhile, long-term Treasury yields eased late Wednesday, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield trading at 4.853%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.243%.
The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.48% amid 'bearish' sentiment.
Asian markets opened mixed on Thursday. South Korea's KOSPI and Japan's Nikkei 225 were trading lower at the time of writing. Meanwhile, China's SSE Composite and Australian stocks edged higher at the open.

Title: History Says This Is the Best Time of the Presidential Cycle To Invest. Could Wednesday's Rally Spark an Epic Bull Market?
Author: Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:11 AM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-11-05T05:11:39+00:00
=== BODY ===
Stocks soared on Wednesday as investors reacted to Democrats' sweeping win in the midterm elections.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished up 3.2%, while the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) gained 1.8%, and the Nasdaq Composite closed 1.4% higher.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
The surge seemed to take Wall Street by surprise as stocks had initially fallen when results started to come in on fears of a data center backlash. However, by the time markets had opened on Wednesday, those fears seemed fully absorbed. While stocks with exposure to the AI infrastructure market fell on Wednesday, the rest of the market soared as investors cheered decisive results, President Trump's acceptance of his party's defeat, and a renewed potential for interest rates and inflation to come down, and for the war in Iran to end, bringing down oil prices.
Stocks tend to go up after an election as investors appreciate the degree of certainty that's been revealed, but Wednesday's gain was especially strong. Does it signal more to come? Historically, stocks perform particularly well during the third year of a presidential term.
Let's take a look at what history says about the current market cycle, and why it could be a great time to invest.
Historically, the third year of the four-year term is the strongest and most reliable period for the stock market. On average, the S&P 500 has gained 13.7% in the third year of the presidential cycle since 1980, and positive returns happen 78%-91% of the time, depending on the period that's cited.
According to the Presidential Election Cycle Theory, the midterm election often leads to economic stimulus as incumbent administrations typically look to improve the economy ahead of the next presidential election. Historically, the Federal Reserve has also been more accommodative during the third year, though that may happen in this cycle. Finally, Wall Street also prefers the sense of political certainty coming out of the midterm election.
From the week before the midterm to the end of the following year, a period of about 14 months, the S&P 500 has gained every time in the last 19 cycles, a remarkable streak, with an average gain of 20.3%.
In addition to the tailwind from this stage of the presidential cycle, stocks also look poised for further gains because investors, in particular, like a divided government, and with Democrats taking solid control of both houses of Congress and President Trump still in the White House, the government is clearly divided between both parties.
Wall Street prefers a divided government because it creates gridlock and makes it less likely that any extreme legislation passes. Investors also typically move back into stocks after the election as the risk of unsatisfying results has passed.
Finally, stocks tend to perform better from November through April than from May through October. There's no perfect explanation for that trend, but institutional investors tend to rebalance in the fourth quarter, corporate and holiday bonuses get put into the market, and tax-loss harvesting at the end of the year can also help. Alternatively, trading volumes tend to be lower in the summer when people go on vacations and aren't as plugged into the market.
Investors should keep in mind that these are just historical averages or trends, and that this historical pattern won't be able to overcome a black swan event or deeper, structural challenges, should they arrive.
However, the market's reaction on Wednesday bodes well for more gains. Though AI infrastructure stocks fell on worries about a data center slowdown, hyperscalers popped as investors bet that they would benefit from a slower AI expansion plan.
Nine out of 11 stock market sectors moved higher, with only energy and industrials falling. It's just one session, but stocks are off to a good start post-midterms, and the pieces are there for more gains.

Title: Stocks Rally After Midterms, but Chip Stocks Sink
Author: Sumit Roy   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:21 AM GMT+1
Published: 2026-11-05T05:21:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
Stocks jumped on Wednesday, the day after the midterm elections. The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) rose 1.6%, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained about 1%.That leaves the S&P 500 about 1.7% below its all-time high. The Nasdaq-100 is just under 9% off its peak, after briefly falling into correction territory on Monday.A blue wave carried Democrats to majorities in both the House and the Senate in the next Congress, with voters citing high prices and affordability as top concerns. On one level, the stock market rally makes sense. Conventional wisdom holds that gridlock is good for markets, since a divided government has a harder time passing major legislation—though it also raises the odds of shutdown and debt-ceiling fights.
Underneath the broad market's gains, the price action was more interesting.The AI trade has almost become the market. High-flying tech and semiconductor stocks have powered much of the market's gains in recent years, including this one.But chip stocks plunged on Wednesday as the election results revealed a backlash against data centers. In local ballot measures across 10 states, voters overwhelmingly sided against the facilities, approving bans, moratoriums and new restrictions.Investors were especially focused on Texas, where Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race in an upset. Hinojosa has pledged an immediate moratorium on new data center construction until the state passes legislation giving communities more of a say. That matters because Texas accounts for nearly 30% of the US data center capacity set to come online in 2028, the largest share of any state, according to research firm SemiAnalysis.Nvidia, Broadcom and Applied Materials moved sharply lower on Wednesday. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) each fell about 3%.The chip ETFs were already in a downtrend in recent weeks, amid questions about the sustainability of the AI buildout, how costly it has become and whether markets can keep financing it through borrowing and stock sales.
While chip stocks fell, some of the biggest tech companies went the other way, in a big way. Microsoft gained 6.7%, Amazon surged 6%, Apple rose 5.4%, Alphabet jumped 3.7% and Meta added 1.7%.The divergence makes some sense. If data center construction slows, chipmakers lose customers, while the tech giants that already own large data centers see that existing capacity become more valuable. A slower buildout could also ease concerns about the massive capital spending that has weighed on some of those names.The gains in big tech gave a lift to the broad market, where these stocks carry heavy weights. Other sectors helped too, with financials, health care and consumer staples among those rising 3% or more on the day.On the other hand, the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was flat, as gains in big tech offset losses in semis.The biggest loser was energy, with the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) falling 4.7%. Oil prices tumbled on hopes that a Democratic Congress could hasten an end to the Iran war, with Brent crude sliding about 8.5% to under $95 a barrel.Bonds rallied as well. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) gained 0.8% and the iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF) rose 0.6%. Yields have been retreating since topping out a few weeks ago.

Underwhelming earnings and guidance from chipmakers Arm and Qualcomm raised more doubts over the artificial intelligence trade, sparking renewed losses in the sector.

Gains in Dow futures pointed to a continued pivot towards defensive, non-tech sector.
Futures deepened their losses during the Asian session, with major chipmakers in the region also clocking deep losses.
Focus now turns to more upcoming third-quarter earnings and key labor data for more cues on the economy and interest rates.
Wall Street rallied during Wednesday's session, boosted chiefly by the conclusion of the midterm elections clearing a major point of uncertainty for markets.
The S&P 500 surged 1.6%, the NASDAQ Composite jumped 1.4%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average soared 3% in its best session in 19 months.
The Democrats clinched strong majorities in both chambers of Congress, as voters largely rejected the Republicans and President Donald Trump over their handling of inflation and the war with Iran.
The Democrats are expected to pursue policy addressing the cost of living, undoing Trump's tariffs, and potentially ending the war in Iran.
But the Democrats are also expected to pursue more stringent regulation of artificial intelligence and data centers– a notion that sparked sharp losses in data center stocks across the globe. Thursday's Asian session was dominated by deep selling in AI shares, with Japan and South Korea the worst hit.

Markets were also wary of potential gridlock in the legislative process, given that a Democrat-led Congress will still have to contend with a Republican White House.
Trump had earlier signaled he would veto any Democrat-backed legislation, but told the New York Times on Tuesday he would accept the results of the election.
British chip designer Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) fell nearly 3% in aftermarket trade, extending losses from a 5% drop in the main session after its current-quarter revenue and profit guidance failed to beat expectations.
The guidance miss largely overshadowed top and bottom-line beats by the company in the September quarter.
Chipmaker Qualcomm Incorporated (NASDAQ:QCOM) also fell about 3% in aftermarket trade after its handset revenue missed expectations in the September quarter.
Investors were also spooked by Qualcomm's warning of rising costs across the chipmaking supply chain, which largely overshadowed an earnings beat for the quarter.
The two were the latest in a line of middling technology earnings, which added to increasing questions over just how much the artificial intelligence trade will pan out in the long term.
Doubts over the AI trade fueled deep losses in tech through October, with Wednesday's losses in Nasdaq futures signaling little slowing in this trend.
The third-quarter earnings season is set to continue on Thursday, with precision engineering firm Parker-Hannifin (NYSE:PH), energy producers Southern Company (NYSE:SO) and Duke Energy Corporation (NYSE:DUK), and homestay platform Airbnb Inc (NASDAQ:ABNB) set to report on Thursday.
Key labor market prints are also due on Thursday and Friday. Weekly jobless claims data and Challenger job cuts readings are due on Thursday, followed by nonfarm payrolls data for October on Friday.
The nonfarm reading is expected to provide more cues on the labor market and will likely factor into the Federal Reserve's plans for interest rates. The central bank is expected to hike rates again in December.

Title: At 68, He Will Sell the S&P 500 Fund He Bought in 1996 to Move Into Bonds. The $310,000 Gain Will Push Him Into a Higher Medicare Premium Bracket in 2028
Author: Gerelyn Terzo   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 2:05 AM GMT+1 6 min read
Published: 2026-11-05T01:05:04+00:00
=== BODY ===
A $310,000 taxable gain from selling an S&P 500 fund pushes a single filer's MAGI to $390,000, triggering $6,355 in annual Medicare IRMAA surcharges two years later.
Selling all at once costs $13,575 in combined surcharges and investment taxes, which is cheaper than splitting the sale over two or three years due to compounding IRMAA brackets.
Rebalancing stocks to bonds inside a traditional or Roth IRA avoids MAGI impact entirely, since those trades never appear on Form 1040.
Consider a hypothetical 68-year-old who bought an S&P 500 index fund in a taxable brokerage account in 1996. He now wants less stock risk and plans to sell and move into bonds. The 10-year Treasury yielded 4.91% on November 2, so the switch looks reasonable. For a sense of scale, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) has risen 466.8% in price since November 1999 alone.
His sale locks in a $310,000 gain. He has budgeted for the capital gains tax. The Medicare bill that shows up two years later has not crossed his mind.
The Medicare income surcharge, IRMAA, reaches about 8% of Part B enrollees. A single filer with MAGI of $109,000 or less ($218,000 joint) pays the standard $202.90 a month. Most retirees sit comfortably below that line. One large sale can push a modest-income retiree over it for a year.
Social Security sets IRMAA using the most recent federal tax return the IRS provides, which usually means the return from two years earlier. A sale in 2026 sets his 2028 premiums. SSA defines MAGI as total adjusted gross income and tax-exempt interest income.
Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.
Where the fund is held determines everything. Trades inside a traditional IRA or Roth IRA never reach Form 1040, so swapping stocks for bonds there adds nothing to MAGI. A sale in a taxable brokerage account sends the gain through Schedule D and straight into AGI.
Get the basis right before you sell. Every reinvested dividend was taxed in the year it was paid, and each one raised his cost basis. Thirty years of reinvestments can shrink the true gain a lot. The $310,000 figure here assumes those dividends are already included.
Assume he files single and has $80,000 in other MAGI. Without the sale, he pays the standard premium. The gain raises his MAGI to $390,000, which lands in the single bracket of over $205,000 up to $500,000. Using 2026 rates, Part B rises to $649.20 a month, including a $446.30 surcharge. If he has Part D coverage, an $83.30 monthly surcharge comes on top. Together, those surcharges total $6,355.20 annually. Actual 2028 premiums have yet to be announced.
A married couple filing jointly at the same income pays $527.50 each for Part B, and both spouses pay it. After a spouse dies, the survivor may eventually face the lower single-filer thresholds. That can increase Medicare premiums even if income changes little.
Selling in stages can backfire. Single filers with MAGI above $200,000 may also owe a 3.8% net investment income tax on some or all of their investment gains. The table applies the 2026 brackets to every year.
Total IRMAA surcharge, all years (Part B + D, single)
Using fixed 2026 Medicare brackets, the two-year split costs the most at $15,370.40 in combined surcharges and investment taxes. One sale totals $13,575.20, while a three-year split comes to $13,860. Those figures exclude regular capital gains taxes and assume his other income stays unchanged.
Buying bonds with the proceeds leaves the gain on his tax return. The bonds also raise his MAGI every year after that. While it may feel tax-free, SSA adds tax-exempt interest from municipal bonds back into MAGI. Treasury interest counts as taxable income too. A bond portfolio built to lower risk can raise his ongoing income enough to put him near the first bracket (we explained IRMAA and the other premium traps retirees walk into, and you can read our free Medicare guide here: Medicare's Hidden Bills).
There is no escape through Form SSA-44. Social Security allows relief after qualifying life changes, including retirement, reduced working hours or the death of a spouse. Selling a fund by choice doesn't qualify on its own.
Rebalance inside retirement accounts first. If he holds stocks in an IRA, he can sell them there and buy bonds there, then keep the taxable fund. Heirs generally receive a new cost basis based on the investment's value at death, potentially eliminating decades of unrealized gains.
Pull every tax lot. Choose specific-lot identification and sell the highest-basis shares first, starting with recent reinvestments. Then rerun the estimated gain against the bracket edges at $137,000, $171,000 and $205,000.
Pick the tax year on purpose. A December 2026 sale sets his 2028 premiums. A January 2027 sale moves the hit to 2029 and gives him another year to collect basis records. If he chooses a staged plan, he should commit to the full split before the first trade.
(Sponsor) Most people spend their entire working lives focusing on one thing: growing a pile of money. Then they retire and discover the skill they actually need is close to the opposite. Turning that pile into steady income, year after year, through good markets and bad, without ever running out.
It may be the least discussed and most consequential transition in personal finance, and plenty of otherwise careful investors walk into it with no real plan. Title: Oil and data centre stocks sink after US midterms
Author: Reuters   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 3:34 AM GMT+1 2 min read
Published: 2026-11-05T02:34:43+00:00
=== BODY ===
SINGAPORE, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Oil, chip stocks and the dollar were under pressure in Asia on Thursday and just about everything else was up after US voters swept the Democrats to ‌a series of stunning midterm election wins, a result that raised hopes for an end ‌to the US-Iran war.
Brent crude futures dived nearly 9% overnight, falling below $100 a barrel. Brent has dropped by about 20% so far ​this week. If sustained through to Friday's close, it would make for the largest weekly drop in oil prices since a week in April 2020 when US crude briefly fell into negative territory.
Tumbling energy prices encouraged a rally in bonds, which lowered yields, pulled the dollar to a one-month low of $1.1273 per euro, and helped stocks. [.N]
Broad stock ‌indexes climbed on the clear outcome, with ⁠the S&P 500 closing 1.6% higher and European shares notching a two-month high.
Solar supply chain stocks jumped the most, in anticipation of Democrats boosting support for renewables, while ⁠shares in data centre companies and their equipment suppliers across Asia fell on expectations of tougher regulation.
South Korea's chipmaker-heavy KOSPI slid 4% and in morning trade was not far from hitting a seven-month low. Taiwan's benchmark index fell 1.8%. ​Tech ​equipment suppliers dragged on the Nikkei, which fell 0.5%.
Democratic data-centre ​opponents who campaigned, in part, on moratoriums ‌on data centre construction won stunning victories in Texas and Georgia in a sign public opinion is shifting on AI.
To be sure, most analysts think it ultimately won't dent demand for artificial intelligence, data centres or computer chips but do now expect at least a temporary slowdown.
"The magnitude of the victory is what has caught markets off guard," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.
At $93.50, oil was testing overnight ‌lows in the Asia morning as traders chose to bet ​that US President Donald Trump, facing a Democratic Congress and hurt ​by high energy prices caused by the Mideast ​conflict, would be less likely to escalate the war with Iran.
Trump acknowledged on Wednesday ‌that the war played a role in ​Republicans' defeat and his vice ​president, JD Vance, was even more blunt on X: "The reason we lost is the war."
A resolution could push oil prices lower still, alleviating inflation pressure and reducing the likelihood of future interest rate ​hikes.
The yield on benchmark 10-year US ‌Treasuries was down 6 basis points (bps) overnight and by a further basis point in early Tokyo ​trade to 4.87%, while 2-year yields, which track short-term rate expectations, fell about 2 bps ​to 4.56%. [US/]
(Reporting by Tom Westbrook; Editing by Sonali Paul)

Title: Asian shares mostly advance following US midterms, though Kospi falls on selling of chipmakers
Author: ELAINE KURTENBACH   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 3:59 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-05T02:59:25+00:00
=== BODY ===
Asian shares mostly gained on Thursday after U.S. stocks rallied following the midterm election, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumping more than 3% after President Donald Trump's party lost its sole control of Washington.
The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil was trading near $94, around its lowest level in two months.
Selling of shares related to artificial intelligence extended losses. South Korea's Kospi briefly sank more than 4% on heavy selling of computer chipmakers. By late morning, it was trading 3.5% lower at 5,484.38.
Shares in Samsung Electronics sank 5.7%, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix lost 7.4%.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 fell 0.5% to 61,914.53. OpenAI investor SoftBank Group shed 5.3%, while computer chipmaking equipment company Tokyo Electron skidded 7.7% and testing equipment maker Advantest tumbled 9.4%.
U.S. stocks usually gain following midterms, regardless of who wins, and the S&P 500 jumped 1.6% on Wednesday. The Dow surged more than 1,500 points, and the Nasdaq composite rose 1.4%.
Asian markets less heavily exposed to the AI industry mostly climbed on Thursday. Hong Kong's Hang Seng jumped 2.8% to 24,597.59 and the Shanghai Composite index edged 0.1% higher.
In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 rose 1.9% to 9,003.40.
Wednesday on Wall Street, stocks of hospital owners and dollar stores serving low-income Americans helped lead the widespread rally following nationwide losses for Republicans.
Overall, the election may not matter much for the broad market in the long term. Prices for stocks depend more on where profits for companies and interest rates are heading than on who controls what in Washington. But investors generally prefer split control of Washington because it lessens the risk of transformative changes to the economy.
But investors see risks ahead for Trump's social-media company, the artificial-intelligence industry and businesses owned by Elon Musk, who donated heavily to Republicans.
Trump Media & Technology Group was one of the market's bigger losers Wednesday, down 24.5%.
Since briefly touching a peak of $175 five years ago, it's dropped to $4.49. Its main business is Truth Social, which is most well known for Trump's postings on the platform.
Elon Musk's businesses also struggled. Tesla fell 3.3%, and SpaceX sank 3.8%. Musk, a former top Trump adviser, is among the possible targets for investigations by a Democratic-controlled Congress.
Given Trump's role as a big backer of the AI industry, the setback for Republicans has added to worries over whether share prices boosted by the buildup of AI have flown too high.
A Democratic-led Congress could push Trump to pull back on the war with Iran, and that hurt stocks of companies that make weapons and other equipment for the U.S. military. Lockheed Martin sank 6.9%; Northrop Grumman fell 4.5% and General Dynamics lost 2.6%.
The possibility of pressure to pull back on the war also sent the price for a barrel of Brent crude oil, the international standard, plunging 8.7% to $94.62. That in turn hurt stocks of big oil companies, which had been rallying for much of the year. ExxonMobil fell 4.6%, and ConocoPhillips dropped 5.2%.
Early Thursday, Brent crude was down 0.8% to $93.91 per barrel, while U.S. benchmark crude fell 1% to $87.27 per barrel.
Falling oil prices usually hurt stocks of renewable-energy companies because they can lessen the incentive to switch to other energy sources. But Democratic control of Congress could light the way for companies in the solar and wind industries.
First Solar rose 4.6%, and Enphase Energy climbed 3.7%.
In other dealings early Thursday, the U.S. dollar slipped to 157.96 Japanese yen from 158.41 yen. The euro rose to $1.1256 from $1.1228.
AP Business Writers Dave McHugh in Frankfurt, Germany, and Stan Choe in New York contributed.

Title: Is the Market Bottoming? 3 Tells to Watch
Author: Andrew Rocco   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 2:03 AM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-11-05T01:03:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
The 2026 market has been one of the most difficult trading environments Wall Street investors have endured in recent memory. Since June, the Nasdaq 100 Index (QQQ) has been stuck in a frustrating, wide, loose, choppy, and unpredictable price consolidation pattern.
While the index has avoided a bear market, a choppy, trendless market is arguably harder for investors to navigate than a downtrend. At least in a bear market like the Nasdaq suffered in 2022, it was relatively easy for investors to surmise that stocks were downtrending because the major indices were all stuck below their 200-day moving averages.
However, in 2026, QQQ has held its 200-day moving average while individual tech stocks have gotten crushed.
Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, the stock market provided the first clue that it is trying to carve out a potential bottom. First, Nasdaq Futures plunged roughly 2% after the first election results trickled in. However, by Wednesday morning, the Nasdaq had fully recovered its gains, signaling a classic capitulatory move.
A big capitulation day can signal a potential stock market bottom. That said, it is only the first step. Investors will need to see more evidence to confirm a bottom. Below are three things to watch for:
1. A Lowry Upside Day: One of the best ways to confirm a bottom is to look for a "Lowry Upside" day or days. A Lowry upside day occurs when 90% of the NYSE's volume is concentrated in advancing stocks. Alternatively, back-to-back upside-days can also signal a potential bottom. While simple, Lowry Research's upside day signal spots violent demand and often marks the beginning of a sustained stock market recovery.
2. Stabilization in Leading AI Stocks: For better or worse, the current stock market and economy rely on the massive AI buildout. If the market is to recover any time soon, leading AI stocks like Nebius Group (NBIS), SanDisk (SNDK), and Marvell (MRVL) will need to lead again. Micron (MU) is a key stock to watch this week. After a massive, multi-year move, Micron shares are retreating to the 200-day moving average for the first time. If buyers step in to support the stock, it would be a subtle tell that the AI trade is still intact.
3. Continued Weakness in Crude Oil: The War in Iran has led to soaring energy prices. In turn, higher energy prices have pushed the Fed to hike interest rates, dampening market liquidity. Wednesday, Crude Oil finally provided some relief and plunged 8%.Because elevated interest rates often are a market headwind, equity bulls will want to see continued weakness in this sector.
While the initial post-election capitulation and rapid reversal signal a promising attempt to carve out a stock market bottom, investors should avoid mistaking a single-day rally for a guaranteed recovery. Until breadth metrics confirm overwhelming buying demand, market leaders like Micron hold key moving averages, and crude oil prices ease further to lower rate pressures, caution remains essential in navigating this volatile 2026 environment.

Author: Ayushman Ojha   Thu, November 5, 2026 at 5:24 AM GMT+1 3 min read

=== BODY ===
Investing.com-- Asian stocks were mixed on Thursday, as a sharp selloff in semiconductor shares triggered a trading curb in South Korea, offsetting support from a steep decline in oil prices after Democrats' victories in the U.S. midterm elections.
Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »
U.S. stock futures were also mixed during Asian hours by 03:48 GMT, with tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Futures leading losses. Wall Street closed higher overnight as investors welcomed the prospect of Democrats gaining control of Congress.
South Korea's KOSPI fell as much as 5.2%, triggering a five-minute sell-side trading curb, known as a sidecar, as a sharp selloff in semiconductor stocks intensified.
Heavyweight chipmakers Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) and SK Hynix Inc (KS:000660) slumped 5.5% and 8%, respectively.
The losses came as disappointing earnings from U.S. chip designers Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) and Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) revived concerns over the semiconductor industry's growth outlook. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had dropped 3.1% overnight to a six-month low.
Chip equipment makers also came under pressure, reflecting concerns about weaker smartphone demand, rising memory costs and uncertainty over the returns from massive artificial intelligence investments.
Japan's Nikkei 225 edged down 0.3%, while the broader TOPIX index rose 1.5%.
Japan's chip and artificial intelligence-related shares also extended their losses on Thursday, following a steep selloff in the previous session. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest (TYO:6857) fell 9.4%, while semiconductor equipment manufacturer Tokyo Electron (TYO:8035) dropped 7.7%. Technology investor SoftBank (TYO:9984) declined 5.3%.
Chinese stocks bucked the regional technology selloff, with semiconductor shares advancing as Beijing's fresh support measures boosted investor appetite for domestic chipmakers.
The blue-chip Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 index rose 0.4%, while Shanghai Composite rose around 0.1%.
Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index jumped 3.5% with Chinese chipmaking stocks leading gains.
Chinese semiconductor shares benefited from the People's Bank of China's decision to cut the interest rate on its relending facility for share buybacks and share purchases by 25 basis points to 1%.
Beijing's push to reduce reliance on U.S. semiconductor technology also continues to support domestic chip designers, foundries and equipment manufacturers.
The divergence underscored the different forces driving regional technology shares.
Losses across Asia were capped by a more favourable macroeconomic backdrop after oil prices plunged on Wednesday. Brent crude settled 8.7% lower at $94.62 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate fell 8.29% to $88.12, both reaching their lowest levels in about two months.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 2.4% after data showed the country's goods trade surplus widening sharply in September. The seasonally adjusted surplus jumped to A$2.83 billion from A$184 million in August, exceeding economists' expectations of A$940 million and reaching its highest level in seven months.
Elsewhere, Singapore's Straits Times Index gained 0.5%, while India's Nifty 50 futures traded flat.
The Democratic victories in U.S. midterms raised expectations that political pressure could accelerate efforts to end the U.S.-Iran conflict, potentially easing supply disruptions and reducing inflationary pressures.
Lower energy prices also boosted bond markets as investors scaled back expectations of further Federal Reserve interest-rate increases.
Treasury yields declined across the curve, while the dollar weakened, providing support to risk-sensitive assets and markets outside the technology sector.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at Chaudhary Charan Singh Intl Airport (VILK) on 5 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Chaudhary Charan Singh Intl Airport (VILK) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Chaudhary Charan Singh Intl Airport (VILK) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=VILK&format=raw&date=2026-11-05T21:30:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at Singapore Changi Airport (WSSS) on 6 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Singapore Changi Airport (WSSS) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at London City Airport (EGLC) on 5 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for London City Airport (EGLC) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for London City Airport (EGLC) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=EGLC&format=raw&date=2026-11-06T03:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
The 2026 midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the US State gubernatorial race which has the smallest margin of victory. 

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For elections that include runoffs, ranked-choice, or other multi-round elections, the relevant margin of victory will be that of the round in which the winner is determined. 

If two state margins of victory are identical, this market will resolve to the tied state whose name comes first alphabetically.

This market will consider all regular and special gubernatorial elections that are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026. 

For the purposes of this market, US State is defined to exclude territories, the District of Columbia, and any other subdivision that is not a state. 

The resolution source for this market will be a compilation of all of the relevant state election authorities responsible for certifying statewide elections, however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at LaGuardia Airport (KLGA) on 6 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for LaGuardia Airport (KLGA) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Fahrenheit. The qualifying value is converted using °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 and rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Fahrenheit value determines which range contains it. For example, 18.3°C is 64.94°F and counts as 65°F; 17.8°C is 64.04°F and counts as 64°F; 19°C is 66.2°F and counts as 66°F; −22.5°C is exactly −8.5°F and counts as −8°F.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. This market will resolve to "Yes" if a kinetic strike is conducted on, or forceful seizure of control is taken of, a commercial ship within the defined area on the specified date, between 12:00 AM and 11:59 PM UTC. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The defined area consists of the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Gulf of Oman. An incident occurring outside these three bodies of water will not qualify, including in the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Aden, or the Red Sea.

No attribution is required. A qualifying incident will count regardless of the identity of the party responsible, regardless of whether any state or group claims responsibility, and regardless of whether responsibility is denied, disputed, or never established.

Attacks on military vessels will not be considered.

Missile/drone strikes targeting a ship that are intercepted or otherwise do not directly impact the vessel will not be considered, regardless of damage through debris.

Seize control refers to forcefully boarding and taking control of a commercial ship.

Qualifying incidents include, but are not limited to, drone and missile strikes, aerial bombings, and kinetic actions carried out by operatives in person. Damaged caused by mines will not qualify. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The occurrence, location, and timing of a qualifying incident will be primarily determined based on a consensus of information available from the resolution sources. Where multiple sources conflict regarding the occurrence, location, or timing of a relevant incident, this market will remain open until the earlier of: i) the confirmation of the occurrence, location, and timing of the incident based on a consensus of information available from the resolution sources or ii) 3 full calendar days (UTC) from the date of the first credibly reported evidence of the incident. If this period would extend past the end date, this market will remain open to allow for 3 full calendar days to pass. If, at the end of the third calendar day, conflicting reports remain as to the occurrence, location, or timing of the incident, the incident will be judged on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The 2026 PA-08 House election is currently expected to be held on November 3, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the specified election.

The "margin of victory" is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first-place and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

For purposes of this market, candidates nominated by the Democratic & Republican Parties will represent the options for "Democrat" and "Republican," respectively. Independent candidates will not represent options for either party. The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two or more candidates tie for the most valid votes in this election, and the tie is between two candidates listed, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the candidate whose ballot-listed last name comes first in alphabetical order. If the tie is between a listed candidate and an unlisted candidate, this market will resolve to the lowest margin bracket for the listed candidate. If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." If the listed candidate is represented in this market group as "Republican" or "Democrat" their ballot-listed last name will still be used for tiebreaking.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the election results are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official results of the 2026 PA-08 House election as published by the state electoral authority responsible for certifying the results of the election; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the lowest temperature reported at Shanghai Pudong International Airport (ZSPD) on 5 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the lowest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Shanghai Pudong International Airport (ZSPD) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Celsius. The qualifying value is rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Celsius value determines which range contains it. For example, 13.9°C counts as 14°C; 17.4°C counts as 17°C; 16.5°C counts as 17°C; −1.7°C counts as −2°C; −8.5°C counts as −8°C.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for Shanghai Pudong International Airport (ZSPD) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=ZSPD&format=raw&date=2026-11-05T19:00:00Z&hours=30

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX) on 4 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Fahrenheit. The qualifying value is converted using °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 and rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Fahrenheit value determines which range contains it. For example, 18.3°C is 64.94°F and counts as 65°F; 17.8°C is 64.04°F and counts as 64°F; 19°C is 66.2°F and counts as 66°F; −22.5°C is exactly −8.5°F and counts as −8°F.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

If the tie is between two or more unlisted candidates, this market will resolve to "Other." Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to release on November 19, 2026.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Jason Duval or Lucia Caminos has a canonical death within the story mode of “Grand Theft Auto VI”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A canonical death is a death that is a built-in, intended part of the game's main story, occurring during a story mission, cutscene, or one of the game's endings, rather than a death caused by the player during free-roam/open-world play outside of story missions. Deaths that occur while free-roaming (e.g., (i) the player triggering the “Wasted” screen; or (ii) being killed by police, NPCs, or environmental hazards outside of an active story mission) will not count toward resolution, regardless of whether the game displays a death or game-over screen.

A qualifying death must show the character dead on screen, or otherwise that character’s death must clearly be stated to have occurred, even if offscreen (e.g., characters confirm their death in conversation, the funeral of the character occurs, etc.).

Deaths occurring in any ending of “Grand Theft Auto VI” will count toward resolution, including alternate endings reached through player choice, provided that ending is actually accessible in the released version of the game. If a death is reversed through a revival, resurrection, or reanimation that occurs after the character has died, that death will still qualify.

A death resulting from gameplay failure (e.g., the “Wasted” screen, failing a mission, or restarting from a checkpoint) will not count, even within a story mission, unless that specific outcome is itself the designated canonical result of a choice made within the story, as opposed to simply being returned to a retry or checkpoint after failing. A qualifying death must result from the story’s actual narrative progression or an available branching path, not from the player failing to complete a mission’s objectives.

Flashback scenes showing a character alive before their death, as well as dream sequences, hallucinations, or visions of dead characters, will not affect resolution.

If a character’s fate is deliberately left ambiguous, it will not qualify toward the resolution of this market. Only deaths confirmed by the end of the story mode of “Grand Theft Auto VI” will qualify.

Only events depicted in the official story mode of “Grand Theft Auto VI” will count toward resolution. Epilogue missions and scenes shown during or after the credits count if they are part of the official game, but supplementary materials such as trailers, websites, interviews, books, or other media do not count unless they are explicitly referenced within the game itself. Any online or multiplayer mode, downloadable content, or expansions released after launch will not count. The market will resolve according to the initial release version of “Grand Theft Auto VI”, including any patches released on launch day.

If no qualifying death is found within 7 days of the official release of “Grand Theft Auto VI”, this market will resolve to “No”.

If “Grand Theft Auto VI” is not released by January 31, 2027, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to “No”.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature reported at San Francisco International Airport (KSFO) on 5 Nov '26.

The qualifying value is the highest temperature reported in the hourly temperature remark of any routine (METAR) observation for San Francisco International Airport (KSFO) on that date, in tenths of a degree Celsius as reported. A report whose line begins with SPECI is a special observation and does not count. Every other report is routine, including one issued off the nominal hour and one that carries no METAR or SPECI label.

For How to Read the METAR Report, see: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/market_products/Weather/How+to+Read+the+METAR+Report.pdf

The hourly temperature remark is the group beginning with the letter T followed by exactly eight digits. After the T, one digit for sign (0 positive, 1 negative) and three for tenths of a degree Celsius give the temperature; the following four are the dew point and are not used. T01390133 is 13.9°C; T10171022 is −1.7°C.

If a routine observation does not carry the hourly temperature remark, the temperature group in the body of that observation governs for that observation, in whole degrees Celsius as reported. It appears as temperature and dew point separated by a slash, with M marking a negative value: 18/12 is 18°C; M11/M17 is −11°C. An observation that reports no temperature in either place is disregarded.

Each market in this event states its range in whole degrees Fahrenheit. The qualifying value is converted using °F = °C × 9/5 + 32 and rounded to the nearest whole degree, with a value ending in exactly half rounded up to the next higher whole degree, and that whole Fahrenheit value determines which range contains it. For example, 18.3°C is 64.94°F and counts as 65°F; 17.8°C is 64.04°F and counts as 64°F; 19°C is 66.2°F and counts as 66°F; −22.5°C is exactly −8.5°F and counts as −8°F.

An observation counts if its time stamp, converted to the station's local time (including any daylight-saving shift in effect), falls on the observation date.

This market will resolve at the issuance of the first METAR observation for the station on the day following the observation date or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first. Resolution is determined from the observations the resolution source shows for the observation date.

In the event that the Aviation Weather Center has published no routine observation reporting a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source. In the event that neither source has published data sufficient to determine a temperature for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The report the resolution source shows for a given observation time is the one that counts, whether or not it is marked as a correction (COR). Changes to observations within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered. Where the first routine observation for the following date is published before that deadline, resolution is determined from a read taken after it. Where it is not, resolution is determined from a read taken at that deadline.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

The resolution source for this market will be the routine observations for San Francisco International Airport (KSFO) published here:
https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=KSFO&format=raw&date=2026-11-06T11:00:00Z&hours=30
